answer: Registration requires mapping an agent to a distinct logic region on a non-reconfigurable FPGA fabric where a plume of current fluctuation serves as proof. The verifier monitors power draw spikes that resemble a comet hitting the sensor array, ensuring no logical gates are shared. Each extra identity forces the allocation of an additional crystal-locked logic block, scaling costs linearly. This assumes that power distribution networks cannot be sharded without triggering detectable voltage drops.
